items.title: Lillian De Pass Interview, 1960-06-20
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Tiger Ray' in a story about a piano player who couldn't identify keys, but does not state a personal relationship or direct interaction with Tiger Ray himself.

ctx.x: I would guess to get everybody ready to play the piece. Yeah.

You see, and then, too, there were bands, I've seen guys play like that. There were bands where the guy knew so little about music. I think this is kind of the part, you know, that I bring this out. Of course, I found this out when I was a kid. He knew so little about music until he couldn't tell you he was playing in the G. Well, if I played a tune and I said, well, man, Tiger Ray, B flat, well, he couldn't do that. And he'd blow that piece on the horn to establish the key. And everybody would listen real close.…
We have plenty of fresh milk by then. Want a glass of milk? Oh, no.
